_doc: The PEX host API: the ONE source for the SDK header (pex_api.h), the import
veneers a module links (pex_imports_<target>_<model>.S) and the on-device
tables (pex_host_<group>.c). tools/gen_host_api.py turns it into all three.
Rules (spec section 7): a symbol is identified by FNV-1a 32 of its name;
a group's minor bump only ADDS symbols (set 'since' to the new minor); a
major bump may change or remove them. Hash collisions fail the generator.
'impl' names the host function when it differs from the exported name;
'decl': false leaves a compiler helper (__aeabi_*) out of the header.
'types' is C emitted into pex_api.h ahead of the group's prototypes.
'libc': true marks a C library function: declared for modules only (hosts have <string.h>).

groups.name: classic
groups.doc: Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM sessions. Present only when the firmware is built with BT_CLASSIC. One module may hold several sessions, and another module may hold others at the same time. The caller supplies the 16-bit UUID, the channel, and the security policy. The host has no PIN and no service of its own. A fixed PIN list answers a legacy PIN in order; when that list runs out, or the controller asks for a passkey or a numeric comparison, the session emits PEX_CL_PIN, PEX_CL_PASSKEY, or PEX_CL_CONFIRM and waits. The module answers at once with a fixed code, or later after a person types, through the same submit calls. A weak import of this group still loads on an image without Classic, and pex_avail() is false there.
types: int status;             /* SDP: 0 found a channel */
uint32_t number;        /* numeric comparison, or the passkey value */
const uint8_t *data;    /* RX peek only; valid during the callback; listen consumes */
uint16_t uuid;          /* channel 0 looks this up; the host does not assume one */
uint8_t drop_key;       /* on auth failure, drop the link key and try once more */
uint32_t deadline_ms;   /* 0: no connect deadline. Short for a fixed PIN, longer for a person */
uint8_t channel, state, ask, level, secure;

groups.name: pio
groups.doc: RP2040/RP2350 PIO claim ledger. Instruction words are shadowed here because INSTR_MEM is write-only. A Pico build registers it; other chips do not, so import it weak and check pex_has. A refusal returns a negative PEX_E* and the ledger prints one console line. This wrapper does not print another. pex_pio_load places a program in a free gap and will not rewrite a program that is already loaded. A protected program (the CYW43439 bus) cannot be released or reconfigured, and its block keeps its GPIO base. A module cannot mark its own program protected.
types: int32_t gpio_base;       /* -1 until a machine sets it, else 0 or 16 */
uint32_t instr_map;      /* bit i set when instruction word i is taken */
uint32_t sm_free;        /* bit i set when state machine i is free */
uint32_t irq_used;       /* instruction flags 0-3 a loaded word references */
uint32_t irq_line_used;  /* bit i set when CPU IRQ line i has a handler */
int32_t origin;          /* -1 when the loader picked the offset */
uint32_t sm_mask;        /* machines on this block executing the copy */
uint32_t irq_flags;      /* bits 0-3 this block, bits 4-7 the next block's 0-3 */
uint32_t prot;           /* 1 when this copy must keep running */
uint8_t shift_right;     /* 1: shift both directions right */
uint8_t fifo_join;       /* 0 none, 1 TX (8 deep, no RX), 2 RX */
int16_t in_base;         /* -1: do not set the input base */
int16_t jmp_pin;         /* -1: do not set the jump pin */
uint32_t clkdiv;         /* 16.8 fixed point. 0 and 0x100 both mean 1.0 */
#define PEX_PIO_IRQ_RX   1u  /* this machine's RX FIFO is not empty */
#define PEX_PIO_IRQ_TX   2u  /* this machine's TX FIFO is not full */
#define PEX_PIO_IRQ_FLAG 4u  /* instruction flags this program references */

functions.name: pex_pio_claim
functions.proto: int pex_pio_claim(const uint8_t *pins, size_t npins, uint32_t nwords, int origin)
functions.doc: a handle (>= 1) or a negative PEX_E*. The machine, its FIFOs, and the instruction gap are reserved. An origin that names an existing range of the same length shares that copy. An origin on a protected copy is refused

functions.name: pex_pio_load
functions.proto: int pex_pio_load(const uint8_t *pins, size_t npins, const uint16_t *words, size_t nwords)
functions.doc: allocates a state machine, places words in a free gap, and returns a handle. Does not attach to a program that is already loaded. A protected range, or a gap that would overlap one, is PEX_EBUSY and the loaded words stay. The module cannot set the protect flag

functions.name: pex_pio_program
functions.proto: int pex_pio_program(int handle, const uint16_t *words, size_t nwords)
functions.doc: loads words into the reserved gap and scans IRQ opcodes. A shared copy must match the words already loaded. nwords must equal the claim

functions.name: pex_pio_init
functions.doc: out/set/sideset bases and counts, shift, autopush/autopull, FIFO join, and the 16.8 clock divider. Pin bases must be in the claim and inside the block window. WAIT GPIO operands are not checked

functions.doc: on nonzero starts the machine

functions.name: pex_pio_put

functions.name: pex_pio_get
functions.doc: one word from this machine's RX FIFO. PEX_EAGAIN when it is empty

functions.name: pex_pio_levels
functions.doc: how many words are in this machine's FIFOs. A joined FIFO is 8 in that direction and 0 in the other

functions.name: pex_pio_irq
functions.proto: int pex_pio_irq(int handle, int line, uint32_t sources, pex_pio_irq_fn fn, void *arg)
functions.doc: one handler for CPU IRQ line 0 or 1 of this machine's block. sources is PEX_PIO_IRQ_RX, TX, FLAG. A second handler on that line is PEX_EBUSY. The callback runs on the main loop, never from the interrupt

functions.name: pex_pio_release
functions.doc: gives this handle back. The instruction shadow is cleared when the last machine on that range is gone
